summary: A 1980 specification of the File Transfer Protocol, for moving files between hosts. It replaced RFC 542 and was replaced by RFC 959.

eli5.summary: FTP is a way to send files between computers. This earlier version was later improved.

subtitle: Moving files between computers over a network with commands and data connections.

tldr.problem: Computers need a standard way to send files to each other across a network, handling differences in how systems store and represent data.
tldr.mechanism: FTP separates control (commands and replies) from data transfer: a TELNET connection sends commands, while a separate data connection carries the file bytes in chosen modes and types.
tldr.outcome: Applications can transfer files reliably between different systems, with support for ASCII, binary, and other data types. RFC 959 later expanded the specification.

today: RFC 765 is a historical FTP specification from 1980. RFC 959 superseded it with an expanded version that became the standard FTP definition used for decades.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) lets application programs send files between computers on a network. It was designed to be simple and practical, working with different types of computers, from mainframes to minicomputers. The protocol handles differences in how systems store files and lets programs transfer data reliably.
sections.eli5: FTP lets one computer send a file to another computer. It works even if the computers store files differently inside.

sections.title: The FTP Model
sections.content: FTP separates control from data transfer. A TELNET connection (the control connection) carries FTP commands from the user's protocol interpreter (PI) to the server's PI, and replies flow back. The server's data transfer process (DTP) opens a separate data connection to send or receive the actual file bytes. The user can initiate a transfer to a different server; the data moves between the two servers while the user's commands control both.
sections.eli5: Think of FTP as two separate conversations: you give orders over one line, and the file travels over a different line.

sections.title: Transfer Modes and Types
sections.content: FTP offers three transmission modes: Stream mode sends data as a simple byte stream; Block mode wraps data in headers with length and status codes (for restart markers and error tracking); Compressed mode reduces the data size. The RFC also defines representation types: ASCII (text characters), EBCDIC (for IBM systems), and binary (raw bytes). Senders and receivers transform data to handle differences in word length and storage format on different systems.
sections.eli5: FTP can send files three ways: as a plain stream, as labeled blocks, or squeezed smaller. It also knows how to translate between computers that store text differently.

sections.title: Commands and Access
sections.content: FTP uses simple commands to control file operations. The USER, PASS, and optional ACCT commands provide access control. Commands like RETR (retrieve a file) and STOR (store a file) specify the file operation, along with transfer parameters. The server replies with a code (like 230 for success or 332 for needing an account) followed by a text message. Commands can change the current directory, list files, delete files, and abort transfers.
sections.eli5: You log in with a username and password, then type commands like 'get this file' or 'send that file'. The server sends back yes or no.
